item.text: {"summary":"Flowering plant native to southern California and Baja California, chaparral yucca forms a stemless rosette of rigid, sharp-pointed, finely toothed leaves. Its single flower stalk grows extremely quickly and carries hundreds of fragrant white to purplish flowers; the flowering shoot usually dies afterward, while most subspecies produce basal offshoots. Before European settlement, Native Americans ground its seeds into flour and ate pit-roasted hearts, roasted stalks and often parboiled petals.","humanEdibility":"yes","edibilityNote":"Before European settlement, Native Americans ground seeds into flour, pit-roasted hearts, roasted slightly bitter stalks and often parboiled petals.","evidence":{"summary":["s1:p3","s1:p4","s1:p5","s1:p11","s1:p16"],"humanEdibility":["s1:p16"]}}
